violations.why: The higher-priority communicate ISR can reset tickCounter between the measure ISR's increment and its read, so the saved value is wrong.
The communicate ISR's write to tickCounter can land between the measure ISR's read and its later overwrite, so the measure ISR's write replaces the new value.
The increment is a read-modify-write. The communicate ISR can preempt it, and its write to intervalCounter is then lost.
The communicate ISR can reset numberOfRecords after it was used as the index at line 83 and before line 85 reads it again. The two reads then see different values.
The measure ISR writes numberOfRecords back from a value that is stale because the communicate ISR reset it in between. The record is stored at the old index and the reset is overwritten.
